focus.jnote: The backdrop turned defensive, and the scan came up empty — that is the whole story today. The S&P 500 fell ~0.52% Monday to ~7,745, its worst day of August, as oil and yields jumped on renewed U.S.–Iran fears; the Nasdaq slipped ~0.32% and the Dow lost ~273 points. This morning S&P futures are down ~0.4–0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures ~1.1%, dragged by a memory-chip pullback (Micron, SanDisk). The catalyst: the 60-day U.S.–Iran ceasefire expired Monday without a deal, President Trump ruled out an extension and threatened Oman, and overnight a cargo vessel was reportedly struck in the Strait of Hormuz — sending Brent to $91 and WTI to ~$84. The VIX popped ~6.6% to ~15.2. But the full-universe scanner boarded no names across all three setup types. With nothing to underwrite, there is no trade to make.
focus.notdown: No bullish single-name boarded. The Type A earnings scan (81 reporters → 6 in-universe → 3 gaps confirmed → 0 boarded) and the Type C breakout scan (1,064 examined → 421 within-proximity → 3 breakouts confirmed → 0 boarded) both came up empty on quality/validation into a risk-off, gap-down open. Do NOT invent a setup from the headlines — if the scan didn’t board it, it isn’t a Sniper today. Stand aside.
focus.notup: No bearish single-name boarded either. The Type B scan found only 2 universe tickers with a catalyst and none confirmed a gap that cleared the bar. Energy (XLE, XOM) is the one group with a bid on the oil spike, but that is a two-sided war trade — one de-escalation headline gaps it straight back down. Selling anything into an expiring-truce, oil-shock tape with no confirmed name is not a Sniper. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? The gap-risk numbers are borderline — composite 52 (WARM) and P(≥1% gap) ~34%, just under the 35% trigger — but a GREEN light means deploy normal size, and there is nothing to deploy into: the scanner boarded zero qualifying setups. On top of that, the just-expired U.S.–Iran ceasefire, a struck vessel in Hormuz, Brent at $91, and the 30-year yield at a near-two-decade high keep an open-ended tail alive. Not RED, because the numbers are still short of the HOT/≥35% locks and the tape is orderly, not panicked — but the honest stance is YELLOW: no new credit spreads today, keep cash, and re-run the scan tomorrow pre-open.
